newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Big Sri Lanka tea exporter set to raise capacity.
newsitem.headline: Big Sri Lanka tea exporter set to raise capacity.

text.p: MJF Group, Sri Lanka's biggest exporter of value-added teas, said on Wednesday it plans to expand production by installing more high speed teabagging machines at a cost of $10 million.
Production capacity was full despite the setting up of a new plant in 1995, it said in a statement.
The statement said the group exported 17.3 million kg of tea in teabags and packets valued at 2.9 billion rupees last year, 95 percent of it under its own Dilmah brand.
"It is very rare for a company in a Third World country to market its commodity under its own brand name," a company spokesman said.
Most other exporters pack foreign-owned brands, Tea Board officials said.

Sri Lanka, the world's leading tea exporter, still exports most of its tea in bulk as it has done for over a century. But exporters were gradually realising the importance of selling value-added products, they said.
The group exported 3.4 million kg of tea in tea bags, which has the maximum value addition, earning more than a billion rupees, the statement said.
"Record demand for Dilmah tea is a major contributor to high prices of Ceylon tea since mid-1996," it added.

Tea prices soared to record high late last year mainly because of strong winter demand for the distinct low grown teas from the Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS), the Indian Ocean island's biggest tea market, and the Middle East.
Russia and other CIS members bought nearly 47 million kg directly from Sri Lanka last year, up from 40 million kg in 1995.
Sri Lanka exported a record 244 million kg of tea last year, compared to 240 million kg in 1995.
